Sodium lauryl sulfate, in turn, is associated with Potassium-transporting ATPase subunit beta. This suggests a possible pathway where Chakasaponin Iii may modulate the activity of Potassium-transporting ATPase subunit beta through its interaction with the potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily D member 3. The evidence implies a potential regulatory mechanism involving potassium channels and their associated ATPases, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be elucidated. The strength of the evidence is moderate, as it is based on a single score and a chain of indirect relationships, which may not fully capture the complexity of the biological interactions.
